default.notes: Visa-free for tourism for up to 90 days within any 12-month period — the allowance is cumulative across visits, not per entry. An extension of up to 90 further days can be requested from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for a fee.

groups.notes: Andean Community (CAN) citizen — enter on a national identity card under the Andean Migration Card, normally with up to 180 days granted.

One of the few nationalities excluded from Ecuador's visa waiver — a consular tourist visa must be obtained before travel. Ecuador revises this list frequently, so confirm the current position with a consulate.

EC.notes: Home country — no entry requirements for Ecuadorian citizens.

CN.notes: Ecuador suspended its visa waiver for Chinese citizens in mid-2024 over irregular migration, and the suspension remains in force — apply for a consular tourist visa and confirm the current position before booking.

VE.notes: Venezuelan citizens have needed a visa for Ecuador since 2019, and requirements were tightened again in 2024 — apply at an Ecuadorian consulate well ahead of travel.

AR.notes: Visa-free for 90 days within any 12-month period; as a Mercosur citizen you may enter on a national identity card and can apply in-country for temporary residence under the Mercosur residence agreement.

BR.notes: Visa-free for 90 days within any 12-month period; as a Mercosur citizen you may enter on a national identity card and can apply in-country for temporary residence under the Mercosur residence agreement.

PY.notes: Visa-free for 90 days within any 12-month period; as a Mercosur citizen you may enter on a national identity card and can apply in-country for temporary residence under the Mercosur residence agreement.

UY.notes: Visa-free for 90 days within any 12-month period; as a Mercosur citizen you may enter on a national identity card and can apply in-country for temporary residence under the Mercosur residence agreement.

CL.notes: Visa-free for 90 days within any 12-month period; Chilean citizens may enter on a national identity card under the regional agreement.

XK.notes: Ecuador does not recognise Kosovo, so Kosovan passports are not covered by the visa waiver — contact an Ecuadorian consulate before travel, and use a second nationality if you hold one.
